title: Severe Sepsis & Septic Shock
pathophysiology: Dysregulated host response to infection with hemodynamic instability and hypoperfusion.

facts.onset: I started feeling severe shivering and weakness early this morning. I could barely get out of bed.
facts.symptoms: I feel burning when I pass urine, bad pain on my side, shaking chills, and dizziness when I sit up.
facts.history: I take metformin for type 2 diabetes. No known drug allergies.
facts.risk: I feel faint, lightheaded, and my hands feel clammy.
facts.exam: Patient is febrile, tachycardic, hypotensive, with delayed capillary refill (> 3 seconds).

blood-culture.name: Blood cultures (2 sets)
blood-culture.result: Collected prior to antimicrobial administration; Gram-negative bacilli isolated in preliminary report.
blood-culture.interpretation: Supports bacteremic source; guide targeted antimicrobial therapy.
blood-culture.why: Identify causative pathogen before starting broad-spectrum empiric antimicrobials.

blood-gas.name: Venous blood gas & Lactate
blood-gas.result: pH 7.28, PaCO2 30 mmHg, HCO3 14 mmol/L, Lactate 4.2 mmol/L.
blood-gas.interpretation: High-anion-gap metabolic acidosis with hyperlactatemia (> 4 mmol/L) indicating tissue hypoperfusion.
blood-gas.why: Assess metabolic severity, tissue perfusion and response to resuscitation.

fbc.name: Full blood count
fbc.result: WBC 21.4 x 10^9/L with 88% neutrophils; Platelets 110 x 10^9/L.
fbc.interpretation: Severe leukocytosis and consumptive mild thrombocytopenia consistent with severe sepsis.
fbc.why: Assess hematological response and thrombocytopenia risk.

renal-electrolytes.name: Renal function & Electrolytes
renal-electrolytes.result: Creatinine 185 umol/L (baseline 80); Urea 14.2 mmol/L; Sodium 134 mmol/L; Potassium 4.8 mmol/L.
renal-electrolytes.interpretation: Acute Kidney Injury (AKI Stage 2) secondary to septic hypoperfusion.
renal-electrolytes.why: Assess end-organ renal dysfunction and guide fluid resuscitation.

ct-head.name: CT head
ct-head.result: Not performed; no focal neurological signs or history of head trauma.
ct-head.interpretation: Not indicated as an initial investigation for septic shock without focal neurological deficit.
ct-head.why: Resuscitation takes absolute priority; unnecessary transfer for imaging is unsafe.

expected_actions: ABCDE assessment and high-flow oxygen per protocol
Rapid IV crystalloid fluid resuscitation (30 mL/kg)
Measure and serial monitoring of lactate
Urgent escalation to Senior Intensivist / ICU team
critical_errors: Delaying broad-spectrum IV antimicrobials beyond the golden hour
Failing to administer urgent fluid resuscitation for hypotension and hyperlactatemia
Sending an unstable patient to unmonitored CT before hemodynamic stabilization
